documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Steady since the fall admission. Weighs every morning, 184-186. Walks indoors at the mall when it is icy. No orthopnea, no chest pain. Strength fine.

Meds: lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, metformin 1000 BID, furosemide 40, ASA 81, prednisone 5, azathioprine 100, acetaminophen PRN.
Allergies: hydrochlorothiazide (angioedema, electrolyte abnormalities).

O: Vitals reviewed. Lungs clear. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P: HFrEF/cardiac amyloid compensated; HTN, T2DM, CKD 3b, polymyositis and AL amyloidosis surveillance stable. A1c, CMP, CBC today (also azathioprine monitoring). RTC May for wellness visit.

Problems reviewed: HTN; T2DM with CKD; CAD s/p LAD stent; HFrEF with cardiac AL amyloid (ADHF admission 10/2024); systemic AL amyloidosis in surveillance; polymyositis in remission; CKD 3b; lumbar spinal stenosis; oropharyngeal dysphagia; prior stroke with mild left arm/hand weakness.
Meds: lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, metformin 1000 BID, furosemide 40, ASA 81, prednisone 5, azathioprine 100, acetaminophen PRN.

Exam: lungs clear, heart regular, no edema. Timed up-and-go normal.

Prevention: flu and updated COVID in the fall. Pneumococcal, shingles and RSV complete. Labs: lipids, BMP, urine albumin/creatinine.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY - CARDIOLOGY / CARDIAC INTENSIVE CARE
Admitted: 11/04/2025   Discharged: 11/10/2025

Presentation: 73-year-old man with systemic AL amyloidosis with cardiac involvement and chronic HFrEF, admitted with two days of rapidly worsening breathlessness. He needed three pillows to sleep and could not walk a block before stopping for fatigue and air hunger. He said it felt like last October's episode. No chest pain, fever or intercurrent illness.

PMH: CAD s/p LAD stent; CKD 3b; hypertension; type 2 diabetes; polymyositis in remission; lumbar spinal stenosis; oropharyngeal dysphagia; prior ischemic stroke with mild left-sided weakness; hepatic dysfunction 2023 (resolved).
Home medications: lisinopril 20 mg, amlodipine 5 mg, metformin 1000 mg BID, furosemide 40 mg, aspirin 81 mg, prednisone 5 mg, azathioprine 100 mg.
Allergies: hydrochlorothiazide (angioedema, electrolyte abnormalities).
Social: never smoker, no alcohol, retired accountant.

Admission exam: T 36.8 C, BP 155/95, P 95, RR 22, SpO2 93% on room air. S1 and S2 normal with an S3. Crackles at both bases. JVD. No peripheral edema. Fundi: arteriolar narrowing, no papilledema.

Diagnosis: acute decompensated heart failure in amyloid cardiomyopathy.

Course: admitted to the cardiac ICU for close monitoring and IV diuresis; transferred to the cardiology floor on hospital day 3 once breathing comfortably on room air. Responded well to IV furosemide. Kidney function and electrolytes remained at baseline. Back to his usual walking distance on the unit before discharge.

Discharge medications: unchanged from home.

Follow-up: primary care within 7 days; cardiology clinic in 4-6 weeks. Daily weights; call for 3 lb in a day or 5 lb in a week.

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Transitional care visit after admission 11/4-11/10 (cardiac ICU, then floor) for acute decompensated heart failure. Discharge summary reviewed; RN call 11/11.

S: Breathing back to normal for him, sleeping on one pillow. Walks his driveway and down the road. No chest pain. Home weight 182. Scared by how fast this one came on - did nothing differently that he can identify.

Meds: lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, metformin 1000 BID, furosemide 40, ASA 81, prednisone 5, azathioprine 100, acetaminophen PRN.
Allergies: hydrochlorothiazide (angioedema, electrolyte abnormalities).

O: Vitals reviewed. JVP not elevated. Lungs clear. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P:
1. ADHF - resolved; second admission in about a year. Euvolemic on furosemide 40. Daily weights with call parameters; reviewed early warning signs (needing more pillows, walking less far). Cardiology clinic 12/9.
2. HTN, T2DM, CKD 3b - BMP today.
3. Polymyositis, AL amyloidosis - stable, specialists following.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
CARDIOLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 12/09/2025

Seen after his November admission (cardiac ICU, then floor) for acute decompensated heart failure. Since discharge he is at his dry weight on furosemide 40 mg daily. No orthopnea, no chest pain.

Medications: lisinopril 20 mg, amlodipine 5 mg, furosemide 40 mg, aspirin 81 mg, metformin 1000 mg BID, prednisone 5 mg, azathioprine 100 mg.
Allergies: hydrochlorothiazide (angioedema, electrolyte abnormalities).

Exam: JVP normal. Lungs clear. No edema.

Assessment: Cardiac AL amyloidosis with HFrEF, compensated after a second decompensation.

Plan: no medication changes. Daily weights. Return 12 months, sooner as needed.
